raw_segments.text: Boy, as young as I am, I have observed these three swashers.
I am boy to them all three, but all they three, though they would serve me, could not be man
to me, for indeed three such antics do not amount to a man.
For Bardolph, he is white-livered and red-facked, by the means where Ava faces it out but fights
not.
For Pistol, he hath a killing tongue and a quiet sword, by the means where Ava breaks
words and keeps whole weapons.
For Nim, he hath heard that men of few words are the best men, and therefore he scorns
to say his prayers lest a should be thought a coward.
But his few bad words are matched with his few good deeds, for a never broke any man's
head but his own, and that was against a post when he was drunk.
They will steal anything and call it purchase.
Bardolph stole a loot-case, bore it twelve leagues, and sold it for three half-pents.
Nim and Bardolph are sworn brothers in Filching, and in Calais they stole a fire-shovel.
I knew by that piece of service the men would carry coals.
They would have me as familiar with men's pockets as their gloves or their handkerchers,
which makes much against my manhood if I should take from another's pocket to put into mine,
for it is plain pocketing up of wrongs.
I must leave them and seek some better service.
Their villainy goes against my weak stomach, and therefore I must cast it up.
